picked.t: Vietnam no longer Japan's largest source of visa overstayers as violations drop
picked.body: Japan's Immigration Services Agency counted 10,260 Thai nationals and 10,135 Vietnamese overstaying as of July 1 in figures released last month. Vietnam had topped the list on Jan. 1 with 11,601 overstayers, ahead of Thailand's 10,907. Both groups shrank, but Vietnamese numbers fell by 1,466 while Thai numbers fell by 647, or 5.9%. The agency attributed the sharper Vietnamese drop partly to the return home of Vietnamese who had overstayed on technical intern visas, Nikkei reported. Overstayers who had held technical intern status numbered 7,928 on July 1, down 1,395 since Jan. 1, the agency's data show. Short-term visitors were the largest category at 39,180, or 60% of the total. Vietnamese still accounted for the most new cases. Of the 6,020 foreigners who began overstaying after Jan. 1 and were still overstaying on July 1, 1,402 were Vietnamese, followed by 1,049 Thais and 611 Indonesians. Vietnamese remain Japan's second-largest foreign community, numbering 693,750 at the end of June behind 941,031 Chinese, out of a record 4,281,026 foreign residents, according to a separate agency release. Thais made up about 15.7% of the 65,229 foreigners overstaying in Japan on July 1, a total down 4.8% from 68,488 at the start of the year. South Korea ranked third with 9,759, and Sri Lanka was the only one of the top 10 countries and territories to post an increase. The decline comes as Japan pursues its Zero Illegal Foreign Residents Plan, unveiled in May 2025 to speed up the removal of foreigners who break immigration rules. Women accounted for about two-thirds of Thai overstayers, at 6,732 against 3,528 men, The Thaiger reported. Thailand's top ranking has raised questions over the visa exemption Japan grants Thai travelers, though Japan has made no official announcement that it will revoke the privilege over the figures. Since July 1, 2013, Japan has allowed Thais with ordinary electronic passports to stay up to 15 days for tourism, business or family visits without a visa.

picked.t: Husband of beauty queen quits job to run $700,000 Vietnamese noodle restaurant in Canada
picked.body: Huong said Lieu previously held a secure, well-paid position at a reputable automotive company and was the family's breadwinner. However, he recently chose to leave the job to help her run the restaurant. The couple plans to work together until the business is running smoothly. Once she can handle operations independently, her husband intends to either pursue further studies in a different field or return to a management position at an automotive dealership. Their restaurant would serve Vietnam's beloved dishes pho and bun bo Hue , on a busy street in Vancouver. Pho , originating from northern Vietnam, is known for its light flavors, often featuring hints of star anise and cinnamon, while bun bo Hue , from central Vietnam, boasts a spicy broth. The restaurant's signage has been installed, but the couple are waiting for an auspicious date to officially open the business. Huong said she had studied the local market and understood the challenges facing Canada's restaurant sector. According to Restaurants Canada, about four in 10 food service businesses are either losing money or just breaking even. Industry analysts have warned that restaurant closures this year could outnumber new openings by thousands, with independent and mid-sized establishments particularly vulnerable. In major cities such as Vancouver and Toronto, high rents, labor costs and insurance premiums are putting additional pressure on restaurant operators. Huong, 36, was crowned Miss World Vietnamese 2010. She also competed in Miss Earth 2010 and reached the top 14.

picked.t: ‘동남아 유일’ 베트남, 3분기 스마트폰 출하량 1% 증가…샤오미 삼성전자 제치고 1위 올라
picked.body: 삼상전자 갤럭시 S26 울트라. (사진=삼성전자베트남) 베트남의 3분기 스마트폰 출하량이 소폭 증가한 것으로 나타났다. 같은 기간 동남아에서 스마트폰 출하량이 증가한 국가는 베트남이 유일했다. 영국 런던에 본사를 둔 시장조사기관 옴디아(Omdia)에 따르면, 3분기 동남아 지역 스마트폰 출하량은 전년 동기 대비 36% 감소한 것으로 조사됐다. 베트남은 1% 소폭 증가했는데, 이를 제외한 나머지 시장은 모두 두 자릿수 감소율을 보였다. 특히 인도네시아와 필리핀, 말레이시아, 태국에서는 출하량이 30% 이상 급감했다. 자세히 살펴보면 동남아 전체 스마트폰 출하량은 작년 3분기 2,560만 대에서 이번 3분기 1,650만 대로 감소했다. 지난 상반기부터 시작된 약세가 이어진 셈이다. 옴디아는 이러한 동남아 시장 전반의 부진의 주된 원인으로 메모리 칩 부족과 부품 가격 상승을 꼽았다. 이 때문에 제조사들이 출하량을 줄이고 제품군을 조정해야 했다는 설명이다. 다만 ASP(평균판매가격)가 전년보다 53% 오르면서 금액 기준 역내 스마트폰 시장 규모는 1% 감소하는 데 그쳤다. 옴디아 관계자는 “경제 성장 모멘텀이 내수 수요를 뒷받침하며 베트남 스마트폰 시장이 높은 회복력을 보였다”며 동남아 전반의 부진 속 베트남 시장이 상대적으로 선방한 배경으로 강력한 경제 성장을 꼽았다. 시장 점유율에서도 유의미한 변화가 관측됐다. 중국 제조사 샤오미가 점유율 27%로 삼성전자를 근소하게 앞서며 처음으로 베트남 최대 스마트폰 브랜드가 된 것이다. 샤오미에 1위를 내준 삼성전자는 약 27%를 나타냈으며, 뒤이어 애플 19%, 오포(Oppo) 16%, 비보(Vivo) 6% 순을 나타냈다.

picked.t: Vietnam seen as one of Southeast Asia's most dynamic F&B markets
picked.body: "The country is a major supplier of coffee, seafood, rice, cashew nuts, tropical fruits and spices," Henri Tan, managing director of SIAL Network – ASEAN & India, said on the sidelines of the inaugural SIAL Vietnam 2026 in Ho Chi Minh City last week, describing Vietnam as "one of Southeast Asia's most dynamic F&B markets." "Its strong agricultural production, expanding food processing capabilities and growing domestic market make Vietnam attractive to international buyers seeking quality products and reliable suppliers," he told Vietnam News and Law . However, attracting buyers is only part of the challenge. Vietnamese producers also need to invest in processing, product development and branding to capture more value and compete in higher-value market segments. Moving beyond raw exports Vietnam has considerable room to increase the value of its food exports. Many businesses still focus on raw materials, while processing, branding and distribution could help them capture a greater share of supply-chain value. Dr. Dinh The Hien, director of the Research Institute of Informatics and Applied Economics, said raw materials accounted for around 5-10% of total value along the food supply chain, compared with 50-70% for distribution and retail. The estimates show why export growth alone may not be enough: businesses also need stronger processing capabilities and better access to overseas markets. International buyers are increasingly looking for traceability, consistent quality, clear product origins and convenience. Tan said processed foods, packaged snacks, ready-to-eat products and specialty beverages could offer opportunities beyond Vietnam's established exports. For small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), having a good product was only the starting point. Understanding overseas market requirements, finding suitable distributors and building relationships with reliable buyers were equally important, he said. Coffee seeks higher value The coffee industry illustrates the move beyond raw exports. Vietnam is a major producer, but the next step is to develop processed products and brands that can compete globally. Nguyen Nam Hai, chairman of the Vietnam Coffee - Cocoa Association, said the industry's priority over the next five years was to move higher up the global coffee value chain. This would require investment in advanced processing, new products and Vietnamese brands with international appeal. The aim was to build on the country's production strength by improving quality, sustainability and value creation, allowing growers and businesses to retain more value from their products, he said. Hai said international buyers were attracted by Vietnam's ability to supply coffee in large volumes while offering distinctive products from different growing regions. He also saw the exhibition as an opportunity for domestic coffee businesses to introduce new products and meet overseas buyers. Building Vietnamese brands Developing recognizable brands and meeting international quality requirements remain major challenges for local food producers. Recognition of Vietnamese cuisine does not automatically translate into demand for Vietnamese food brands. Producers still need consistent quality, meet food safety and sustainability requirements, and stand out from established competitors. Smaller businesses may struggle to afford new technology, obtain international certifications and establish overseas distribution networks. Bui Hong Hanh, founder and CEO of Vietnamese chocolate maker Legendary Chocolatier, said the company combined Vietnamese cacao with local ingredients to produce distinctive chocolates. The company exports to markets like Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Canada and Hong Kong, and is seeking to expand into North America and Europe. Building brand recognition overseas, meeting different market requirements and competing with established global brands while keeping prices competitive remained difficult, she said. The company continued to invest in research and development, manufacturing technology and quality control, as well as products and packaging that reflect Vietnamese culture. Barbara Jankiewicz, business development manager at Poland-based consulting firm MDelta, said the country's growing consumer demand and role in regional food supply chains offered opportunities for international businesses. Tan said SIAL Network could help Vietnamese SMEs better understand overseas markets and connect with potential buyers. Established in Paris in 1964, the SIAL Network organizes food industry exhibitions in several international markets. Its first Vietnamese edition took place from Nov. 11-14 alongside the Vietnam Foodexpo 2026 in HCMC. But turning contacts into lasting business relationships will depend on whether they can meet international standards, maintain consistent quality and offer competitive products. picked.t: Hanoi hosts global festival to promote traditional craft villages
picked.body: Hanoi is hosting the first Global Craft Village Conservation and Development Festival 2026, bringing together representatives of the World Craft Council (WCC), international organizations and around 200 artisans and designers. The festival opened on Nov. 13 at the Thang Long Imperial Citadel, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, under the theme "Converging Craft Village Identity-Connecting Global Excellence." Its main program runs through Nov. 16, with related activities from Nov. 12 to 17. Organized by the Hanoi People's Committee and the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment, the event aims to preserve traditional craftsmanship while helping artisans and craft businesses improve product design, reach new markets and build international partnerships. Hanoi has about 1,350 craft villages, including 337 officially recognized ones. They preserve 47 traditional crafts, and the city's handicraft products are exported to 89 countries and territories. Four Hanoi craft villages have received recognition from the WCC: Bat Trang for ceramics, Van Phuc for silk, Son Dong for sculpture and lacquerware, and Chuyen My for mother-of-pearl inlay. Son Dong and Chuyen My joined the network earlier this year. Vietnam now ranks second globally in the number of craft villages recognized by the council, according to organizers. Hanoi plans to seek international recognition for more craft villages to preserve traditional skills and expand market opportunities. Activities began on Nov. 12 with a meeting between the Hanoi Department of Agriculture and Environment, WCC representatives and delegates from the four recognized villages. Participants reviewed the villages' progress, preparations for upcoming WCC assessments and potential long-term cooperation. They also discussed a proposed memorandum of understanding between Hanoi and the council. On Nov. 13, the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment and the Hanoi People's Committee held a welcoming ceremony for international delegations, providing an opportunity for officials and craft organizations to discuss cooperation and cultural exchange. The official opening ceremony took place that evening in front of Doan Mon Gate at the Thang Long Imperial Citadel. Attendees included Hanoi People's Committee Chairman Vu Dai Thang, Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Environment Vo Van Hung, Hanoi People's Committee Vice Chairman Bui Duy Cuong, and Sundeep Kumar, WCC vice president for Asia-Pacific Region and co-chair of its World Craft Cities subcommittee. Ambassadors, international organizations, experts, craft associations and artisans also attended. Speaking at the ceremony, Cuong said craft villages generate jobs, support local livelihoods and preserve Hanoi's cultural identity. He stressed that conservation should cover not only traditional products but also the knowledge, skills and cultural spaces associated with craftsmanship. Passing these skills to younger generations is essential to keeping traditional crafts alive, he said. Cuong outlined the city's priorities for developing craft villages alongside the green and circular economy, tourism and cultural industries. These include improving product design and quality, protecting the environment and preserving local identity. International cooperation in training, design and technology could also help Vietnamese handicrafts reach more overseas markets, he added. Kumar described Hanoi as an important strategic partner and proposed formalizing cooperation through a memorandum of understanding. He also proposed establishing a World Craft Centre in Hanoi to connect artisans, designers, researchers and businesses internationally, and a World Craft Academy where master artisans could teach at universities and design schools. After the ceremony, Vietnamese officials and international delegates toured the exhibition, watched traditional craft demonstrations and met artisans. Activities included pottery demonstrations from Bat Trang ceramic and displays of Van Phuc silk and other handicrafts. The festival is part of Hanoi's broader strategy to develop craft villages as economic and tourism assets. The city aims to increase their production value by about 10% annually from 2025 to 2030. Its priorities include building craft brands, training younger artisans, improving product quality and strengthening the competitiveness of local handicrafts in international markets. The city also seeks to promote environmentally sustainable production and closer links between traditional crafts, tourism and creative industries. Through international partnerships, Hanoi hopes to expand opportunities for craft communities while preserving skills and cultural practices passed down through generations.

picked.t: Hanoi shuts streets around central lake for 6 days for Vietnam's first Culture Day
picked.body: The opening ceremony is set for 7:30 a.m. on Saturday at the Ly Thai To flower garden and the Hoan Kiem Lake pedestrian zone. Vietnam Culture Day, which falls on Tuesday, is a new annual paid public holiday that the country is marking for the first time this year, with more than 400 activities nationwide. A 70-meter pair of dragons modeled on Ly dynasty designs forms the centerpiece of the opening stage beside the lake. From Wednesday to Friday, police ban or restrict vehicles from 11 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily. From 8 p.m. Friday until 6 a.m. Monday, the controls run around the clock. During these hours, all vehicles are banned from Dinh Tien Hoang, Le Thai To, Hang Khay, Le Thach, Dinh Le and Nguyen Xi streets and Dong Kinh Nghia Thuc Square. The ban also covers part of the State Bank square and sections of Le Lai, Trang Tien, Ngo Quyen, Ly Thai To, Hang Dau, Lo Su, Tran Nguyen Han, Luong Van Can, Bao Khanh, Hang Bai and Ba Trieu streets. On the surrounding streets, trucks carrying 500 kg or more and passenger vehicles with 16 or more seats are banned, except buses and vehicles with priority badges, while private cars and motorbikes are restricted. These are Ly Thuong Kiet, Tran Hung Dao, Hai Ba Trung, Le Thanh Tong, Phan Chu Trinh, Tran Quang Khai, Tran Khanh Du, Hue, Hang Bong, Hang Gai, Hang Trong, Nha Tho, Nha Chung, Quang Trung and Nguyen Huu Huan streets, plus the remaining sections of Ngo Quyen, Ly Thai To, Tran Nguyen Han, Le Lai, Ba Trieu and Hang Bai. To avoid congestion, police advise drivers to divert to the ring roads. Traffic between the east or northeast and the west or northwest should cross the Nhat Tan, Long Bien, Vinh Tuy or Thanh Tri bridges and connect to Tran Nhat Duat, Yen Phu and Vo Chi Cong streets or Ring Road 3. Traffic between the north and south is advised to cross the Nhat Tan or Thang Long bridges and follow Vo Chi Cong, Pham Van Dong and Pham Hung streets, Ring Road 2 or Ring Road 3.

picked.t: Thailand’s GDP growth accelerates to 2.9% in Q3, ranks fifth among six Southeast Asian economies
picked.body: Although growth accelerated from 2.4% in the second quarter, it exceeded only that of the Philippines with 2.1% in expansion rate, according to the National Economic and Social Development Council (NESDC). In comparison, Vietnam leads the region with 9.9% growth, followed by Indonesia (5.5%), Singapore (5.4%) and Malaysia (5.3%). Investment and exports were the main drivers of Thailand’s growth. Total investment increased by 11.8% in the third quarter, up from 9.2% in the previous quarter. Goods exports reached $106.38 billion, an increase of 23.6% and the fastest growth in 21 quarters. Global demand for products linked to AI and data centers provided significant support. Although investment and exports offered substantial support, some sectors lost momentum. Accommodation and food services expanded by 1.9%, down from 2.1% in the previous quarter. Foreign tourist arrivals totaled 7.061 million, a decrease of 5%, while domestic tourism by Thai travelers grew by 1.9%. The NESDC forecasts economic growth of 2.0–3.0% in 2027, with a midpoint of 2.5%, according to Thai PBS World. While the outlook points to continued expansion, the forecasts suggest investment and exports will remain key sources of growth. Risks associated with the global economy, conflict in the Middle East, energy prices and trade barriers also warrant monitoring.

picked.t: IFC Hanoi blends Vietnamese inspired design with modern office spaces
picked.body: The flowing silhouette of Vietnam's traditional ao dai and the layered contours of terraced rice fields have inspired the design of IFC Hanoi, an office development in the Tay Ho Tay area. Designed by South Korean consultancy Heerim Architects & Planners, the project incorporates these cultural references into a contemporary building intended to meet the needs of modern businesses. With approximately 59,700 sq.m of net leasable area, IFC Hanoi is currently the largest office development by leasable space in Tay Ho Tay. It offers large floor plates, digital infrastructure and integrated amenities. The building's column-free office floor plates span up to 2,000 sq.m, allowing tenants to configure open-plan workspaces, meeting rooms and collaborative areas to suit their needs. The layouts can also be adapted as businesses grow or change their operations. Daewoo E&C, a South Korean contractor with experience in several developments in Hanoi's Starlake urban area, constructed the project. HanmiGlobal, which has worked on more than 3,200 projects across 66 countries and territories, served as the construction management consultant. The design emphasizes natural light and openness. Office floors have ceiling heights of 2.8 meters and full-height glass facades, while multi-story atriums create visual connections between floors and make the interior feel more spacious. The building has 19 smart elevators equipped with AI technology, operating at speeds of up to five meters per second. Its 15th floor is designated as a refuge area for emergencies. Three basement levels provide parking for cars and motorbikes, as well as electric vehicle charging stations. IFC Hanoi is pursuing LEED Gold certification, which evaluates buildings based on criteria including energy efficiency, water use, materials and indoor environmental quality. The development also features outdoor green spaces on the first and fourth floors, as well as a lounge and co-working area. Beyond office space, the project is being developed as a mixed-use destination combining workplaces, accommodation, retail and services. The five-star Shilla Monogram Hanoi Westlake hotel began welcoming guests on Oct. 23, 2026. A four-story retail podium will accommodate cafes, restaurants and convenience stores. Other components include La Résidence serviced apartments and planned connections to the Ngoai Giao Doan area, Takashimaya and Thiso Mall. These amenities are intended to give office tenants convenient access to accommodation, dining, shopping and other services. As Tay Ho Tay develops into an administrative, diplomatic and business district, IFC Hanoi aims to play a key role in shaping the district’s future as a dynamic business destination.

picked.t: Forbes lists Da Nang among destinations for retirement abroad in 2026
picked.body: U.S. magazine Forbes has included Vietnam for the first time in its annual list of the best places to retire abroad, naming Da Nang and Hoi An among 96 destinations across 24 countries. In its article, "The Best Places To Retire Abroad In 2026," Forbes assessed locations based on living costs, healthcare, safety and quality of life. The magazine described Vietnam as an affordable tropical destination, highlighting its cultural attractions, beaches, dining options and relatively low rate of serious crime. Living costs are approximately one-quarter of those in the U.S., it said. Forbes highlighted Da Nang for its long sandy beaches and mix of coastal scenery, outdoor activities and urban amenities. Residents and visitors can take sunrise walks along My Khe Beach, explore the mountains at Ba Na Hills or spend evenings along the Han River. At Sun World Ba Na Hills, cable cars carry visitors to nearly 1,500 meters above sea level, where temperatures are cooler than along the coast. The mountain attraction features the Golden Bridge, supported by two giant hand-shaped structures, as well as the French Village and Moon Castle. The French Village offers accommodation, dining and entertainment, including coffee and pastries at Eric Kayser, Fantasy Park and the Alpine Coaster. Another attraction is the Son Tra Peninsula, known for its forested mountains and coastal scenery. Along Bai Bac Bay, the InterContinental Danang Sun Peninsula Resort, designed by architect Bill Bensley, offers accommodation amid the natural landscape. The resort was named Asia's best in the 2026 Readers' Choice Awards by Condé Nast Traveler, based on reader votes. In the city center, restaurants, cafes, shops and cultural venues line the Han River waterfront, one of Da Nang's main gathering areas. Bridges, riverside promenades and entertainment venues attract visitors throughout the day. Novotel Danang Premier Han River offers views of the waterfront and access to nearby dining and entertainment. Da Nang also hosts major annual events, including the Da Nang International Fireworks Festival (DIFF), which brings international teams to the Han River for competitions accompanied by cultural and entertainment activities. Travel + Leisure Asia included DIFF in its 2026 list of nine summer festivals worldwide worth experiencing. The 43-day festival attracted more than 2.72 million overnight visitors, up nearly 45% from the previous year, according to the Da Nang Department of Culture, Sports and Tourism. Forbes 's guide also noted that Vietnam does not offer a formal retirement visa, an important consideration for foreigners planning to stay long term. The inclusion reflects international interest in Vietnam's affordability and lifestyle options. For Da Nang, beaches, cultural attractions, resorts and year-round events offer a range of experiences for visitors and prospective long-term residents.

1420회차 및 1425회차 추첨결과. (이미지=비엣로트 추첨결과 갈무리) 베트남에서 로또 2등 당첨자가 무더기로 쏟아져 큰 관심을 받고 있다. 베트남 국영 로또사업자 비엣로트(Vietlott)는 지난 17일 파워 6/55(Power 6/55) 1425회차 추첨에서 잭폿2(Jackpot 2) 당첨자 15명이 나왔다고 밝혔다. 당회차 잭폿2 당첨금은 36억5,000만 동(14.2만 달러)으로, 규정에 따라 당첨자들은 1인당 세전 2억4,300만 동(9,458달러)씩을 수령하게 된다. 잭폿2 당첨 확률은 480만 분의 1로, 통상 한 회차에 1~2장에 그치던 것이 이렇게 몰린 것은 출시 이후 이번이 처음이다. 이번 추첨 결과에는 눈에 띄는 대목이 있다. 비엣로트 추첨결과를 보면 지난 5일 진행된 1420회차는 당첨번호 06-20-34-41-49-52에 보너스 번호 36이었고, 17일 1425회차는 06-20-36-41-49-52에 보너스 번호 34가 나왔다. 두 회차에 추첨 번호 7개가 모두 같고, 34와 36만 주번호와 보너스 번호 자리만 서로 맞바뀐 것이다. 결국1420회차 당첨번호와 같은 숫자 6개를 고른 사람은 이번에 잭폿2에 당첨되는 행운을 얻게 된 셈이다. 비엣로트에 따르면, 당첨자 중 3명은 안장성(An Giang) 출신으로, 나머지 당첨자는 호치민시와 껀터, 탄화성(Thanh Hoa), 닥락성(Dak Lak), 빈롱성(Vinh Long), 칸화성(Khanh Hoa), 푸토성(Phu Tho), 타이응우옌성(Thai Nguyen) 등 전국에서 나왔다. 베트남판 로또복권의 일종인 파워 6/55 복권용지. 파워 6/55는 메가 6/45(Mega 6/45)와 더불어 비엣로트의 주력사업 중 하나로, 전체 55개 숫자중 6개 번호를 맞추는 베트남판 로또 복권이다. 1등 당첨 확률은 2898만9675분의 1로, 동행복권 로또 1등 당첨 확률보다 3.6배 가량 낮다. 2등에 해당하는 잭폿2는 5개 번호와 나머지 49개 숫자 중 보너스 번호 1개를 맞히면 당첨된다. 상금은 최소 30억 동으로, 당첨자가 없으면 해당 회차 누적액의 10%가 당첨금에 더해진다. 비엣로트 통계에 따르면 2016년 번호선택식 복권 판매를 시작한 뒤 지난 6월 말 기준 533명이 메가 6/45 및 파워 6/55에서 10억 동(약 3.9만 달러) 이상의 잭폿에 당첨됐다. 당첨금 총액은 약 12조1,800억 동(약 4억7,410만 달러)이다. 이 가운데 400명 넘는 당첨자는 이른바 ‘벼락부자’ 자리에 올랐다. 비엣로트는 베트남 재무부가 지분 100%를 출자한 국영기업으로, 올해는 2016년 첫 상품 출시 이후 처음으로 10조 동(3억8,920만여 달러)을 넘는 매출 목표를 세운 상태다. 비엣로트의 복권 수익은 각 지방정부 예산으로 편입돼 △보건·의료 △교육 △기후변화 적응 △농촌개발 △공공복지 사업 등에 지원되고 있다.
